examples.japanese: {掃除機|そうじき}で{ゴミ|ごみ}を{吸引|きゅういん}する。
examples.english: To vacuum up dirt with a vacuum cleaner.

examples.japanese: {手術|しゅじゅつ}{中|ちゅう}に{血液|けつえき}を{吸引|きゅういん}した。
examples.english: Blood was aspirated during the surgery.

examples.japanese: {吸引|きゅういん}{力|りょく}の{強|つよ}い{掃除機|そうじき}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a vacuum cleaner with strong suction power.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}を{吸引|きゅういん}する{力|ちから}がある。
examples.english: It has the power to attract customers.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{観光客|かんこうきゃく}の{吸引|きゅういん}に{力|ちから}を{入|い}れている。
examples.english: This area is putting effort into attracting tourists.

examples.japanese: {都市部|としぶ}は{人口|じんこう}を{吸引|きゅういん}し{続|つづ}けており、{地方|ちほう}の{過疎化|かそか}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Urban areas continue to draw population, and rural depopulation is advancing.

notes:
Literally means to suck in or draw in. Used both for physical suction (vacuums, medical aspiration) and figuratively for attracting people or attention.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {吸引|きゅういん}{力|りょく}: suction power; drawing power
- {吸引|きゅういん}{器|き}: suction device, aspirator
- {脂肪|しぼう}{吸引|きゅういん}: liposuction
- {人口|じんこう}{吸引|きゅういん}: population attraction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {吸収|きゅうしゅう}: absorption — takes something in and integrates it, rather than merely drawing it in
- {誘引|ゆういん}: attraction, luring — emphasizes enticement or inducement
- {魅力|みりょく}: charm, appeal — describes the quality itself rather than the act of drawing in
